## Packages

```{r}
#| warning: false
#| message: false
library(tidyverse)
library(tidymodels)
library(scales)
```

## Preparation work

Create `tip_bool` , a boolean version of the original variable `tip` (TRUE or FALSE instead of YES or NO)

Glimpse updated data frame : `my_taxi`

```{r}
#| label: create tip a real boolean (TRUE or FALSE) and glimpse my_taxi
my_taxi <- taxi |>
    mutate(tip_bool = if_else(tip == "yes", TRUE, FALSE))

glimpse(my_taxi)
```

## Question 1

**Is there there a relationship between the distance (in miles) someone travels in a taxi and if they tip or not?**

The distance (in miles) someone travels in a taxi is defined by the variable **`distance`**.

**`distance`** is a continuous numerical variable.

The action of tipping (or not) is defined by the variable **`tip`**.

**`tip_bool`** is a boolean variable.

```{r}
my_taxi |>
    ggplot(aes(x = distance, y = as.numeric(tip_bool))) +
    geom_jitter(height = 0.05, alpha = 0.4) + 
    geom_smooth(method = "glm", method.args = list(family = "binomial")) +
    labs(x = "Distance in miles", y = "Probability of tipping")
```

```{r}
my_taxi |>
    ggplot(aes(x = distance, y = tip_bool, color = tip_bool, fill = tip_bool)) +
    geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.5, show.legend = FALSE) +
    labs(x = "Distance in miles", y = "Tipping (TRUE) or Not Tipping (FALSE)")
```

There seems to be a **positive relationship between the distance someone travels in a taxi and their tipping behavior** : even though most people do tip, we can see that this tendency grows positively when the distance increases.

## Question 2

**Do taxi passengers tend to tip more for the company Chicago Independents than the other companies?**

```{r}
my_taxi |>
    ggplot(aes(y = company, fill = tip_bool)) +
    geom_bar(position = "fill") +
    labs(x = "Tipping ratio", y = "Company name") +
    scale_fill_discrete(name = "Tipping behavior", labels = c("FALSE" = "Not tipping", "TRUE" = "Tipping"))
```

```{r}
my_taxi |>
    mutate(chicago_company = if_else(company == "Chicago Independents", "Chicago Independents", "Other Companies")) |>
    ggplot(aes(x = chicago_company, fill = tip_bool)) +
    geom_bar(position = "fill") +
    labs(x = "", y = "Tipping ratio") +
    scale_fill_discrete(name = "Tipping behavior", labels = c("FALSE" = "Not tipping", "TRUE" = "Tipping"))
```

Yes, taxi passengers clearly tend to tip more with **Chicago Independents** than with other companies:

- not only do they tip more often than the **overall average of other companies**,

- but they also tip more often than passengers of **any individual competing company**
